risk_if_not_implemented: Without Pre-Trained AI & Autonomous Technologies Models, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure (R-SC-1), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Component Impact (R-SC-7), AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure (R-AI-1), AI Data Confidentiality / Integrity / Provenance Loss (R-AI-2), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products (MT-20), Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack (MT-29).

compensating_control_1.name: Anomalous Behavior
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and/or User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solutions to detect and respond to anomalous behavior that could indicate account compromise or other malicious activities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Anomalous Behavior (MON-16) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Pre-Trained AI & Autonomous Technologies Models (AAT-36.7) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Conformity Monitoring
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to validate that Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) conform to the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification: Conformity Monitoring (CPL-05) provides periodic assessment and assurance that compensates for the absence of Pre-Trained AI & Autonomous Technologies Models (AAT-36.7) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
